Subject: Turquoise — request: SLA measurement walkthrough + evidence inventory

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and DevSecOps would like a short workshop to walk through exactly how Redwood measures uptime/latency and how service credits would be calculated. They also want a list of the evidence artifacts you can provide (traces, sampled telemetry, audit logs, synthetic probe results, configuration snapshots).

Can we book 60 minutes next week? Specific asks:
- How you define measurement windows (UTC vs customer timezone, rolling vs calendar).
- What latency percentiles are measured and how (p50/p95/p99; sampling).
- How outages vs transient spikes are classified.
- Example credit calculations for a monthly SLO breach.
- Evidence package we can consume or validate during audit.

Alex Reynolds
Senior Procurement Manager
Turquoise Systems

Marissa —

Quick notes for the workshop prep:
- We'll prepare a concise "measurement matrix" that lists each SLO metric (availability, p95/p99 latency for token generation, embedding latency) and the telemetry source (ingress logs, runtime samplers, synthetic probes).
- For measurement windows, propose we show both rolling 30-day windows and calendar-month examples — Turquoise can pick their preferred approach in the contract.
- For crediting, include both proportional credit (percent of monthly uptime missed -> credit %) and a discrete tiered credit for larger incidents — include examples in dollar terms tied to their committed spend (we can show a sample calculation).
- Evidence package: we can provide 30 days of sampling logs, a zipped trace bundle for incidents, and synthetic probe time-series (CSV). Ops can redact customer identifiers on request.

I will pull the draft matrix and sample logs. Ben — can you export the synthetic probe CSV from QA for examples?

—Karthik

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Turquoise — request: SLA measurement walkthrough + evidence inventory

Attached: sla-measurement-matrix.xlsx (draft) — includes columns: metric, source, retention, sampling rate, normalization rules, example query, artifact filename.

Notes on sampling: we record full ingress logs for all requests for 72 hours, after which we store a deterministic sample for 30 days (1 in 10 for high-throughput customers). P95/P99 are computed on the sampled dataset using reservoir sampling + interpolation to approximate full-population percentiles; for critical audits we can run reprocessing on full logs if the timeframe data is still available.

Also attaching redwood-slo-measurement-summary.pdf — short bullets you can send to the customer ahead of the session.

—Ben

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@turquoisesys.com>
Cc: procurement@turquoisesys.com, devsecops@turquoisesys.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Turquoise — request: SLA measurement walkthrough + evidence inventory

Alex — thanks, all set for Wed 11/18 2:00–3:00pm PST. Meeting invite sent.

Summary of what we'll demonstrate and artifacts we'll provide:
- Measurement windows: both rolling (30-day sliding) and calendar-month windows; primary canonical measurement will be calendar-month for billing/credits unless you opt into rolling in the contract.
- Timezone: all telemetry timestamps are recorded in UTC; we show local timezone offset conversions in the report.
- Latency: we measure p50/p95/p99 on request-to-first-token and request-to-final-token where applicable. For embeddings we measure end-to-end request latency. We compute percentiles on sampled datasets and mark percentile confidence; we call out when reprocessing is necessary for audit-grade precision.
- Outage classification: incidents are classified by impact and duration. Transient spikes (single-minute spike without downstream error) are excluded if they do not exceed configured impact thresholds; sustained errors (e.g., 5+ consecutive minutes with error rate > 5%) are candidate outage windows. We will show concrete SQL-ish queries we run to classify windows.
- Credits: standard example we will demonstrate: if monthly availability < 99.95% then credit = (committed monthly fee) * ((99.95 - observed_availability) / 100). We will show a worked example using your committed spend placeholder. We also present a tiered cap and maximum single-incident credit.
- Evidence: we will provide a packaged artifact set per request: (1) sample ingress logs (CSV), (2) synthetic probe series (CSV), (3) trace bundles for incidents (zipped JSON traces), (4) computation scripts (SQL queries) used to derive metrics. PII can be redacted on request.

Attached are the PDF and the draft matrix Ben prepared. Please let us know if you want any additional artifacts or a different credit formula.

Best,
Marissa

From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@turquoisesys.com>

Subject: Re: Turquoise — request: SLA measurement walkthrough + evidence inventory

Marissa — thanks for the walkthrough today; that was very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from DevSecOps procurement:

1) For the percentile computations: can Redwood commit to retaining full (lossless) ingress logs for at least 30 days for audit reprocessing? Your note about 72 hours of full retention then sampling raised flags. If you cannot retain full logs for 30 days we need to understand how percentile reconstruction is validated.

2) For the credit formula: procurement prefers a published, deterministic formula (we like proportional credit) but we need to confirm the maximum aggregate credits per month and the single-incident cap — can you confirm typical caps?

3) Evidence exchange: could you provide a sample zipped incident trace we can ingest into our tooling (Ops uses Zipkin-style JSON traces)? The trace bundle in the packet was summary-only.

If you can answer the three items in writing we can move to a redline pass this week.

—Alex
Procurement — Turquoise Systems
